shared_contract: All visual concepts must strictly adhere to the offline five-file constraint (index.html, styles.css, app.js, journey.json, README.md) with zero external dependencies or CDNs. Every concept must utilize the core palette of warm parchment (#FDFBF7), deep charcoal ink (#1C1A17), and muted brass (#A38A5E), while maintaining full keyboard navigability, responsive layouts, and robust LocalStorage persistence.

candidates.name: The Ledger Folio
candidates.design_thesis: An editorial, double-page ledger layout resembling a master strategist's bound journal. It prioritizes linear reading, structured horizontal rows, and a highly disciplined typographic hierarchy that feels like a physical ledger book.
candidates.composition: A split two-column desktop layout. The left column is a fixed control panel containing the creation form and a prominent, static 'Leaderboard Index'. The right column is a scrollable vertical ledger of option rows, where each option is presented as a wide, ruled row with inline criteria scoring columns.
candidates.typography: Georgia for all headers and option titles, paired with a high-contrast, tabular monospace font for numbers to emphasize the ledger-style mathematical precision.
candidates.interaction_emphasis: Focuses on smooth vertical scrolling, subtle ink-bleed hover effects on interactive rows, and tactile 'ink-stamp' active states when scoring.
anti_goals: No floating action buttons or floating cards.
No modern rounded pill tags for scores.

candidates.name: The Triptych Atelier
candidates.design_thesis: A modular, three-panel architectural layout inspired by drafting boards and folding triptych planning screens. It emphasizes clear spatial zoning and fine brass-ruled borders to separate distinct tasks.
candidates.composition: A three-column grid on desktop. Column 1 houses the criteria configuration and entry forms. Column 2 displays the active options as a dense grid of vertical cards. Column 3 is dedicated entirely to the 'Leader Monolith' and real-time score distribution charts.
candidates.typography: Baskerville for headers to evoke classical drafting archives, paired with an ultra-clean, light geometric sans-serif for inputs and labels.
candidates.interaction_emphasis: Focuses on horizontal card transitions, subtle brass-inlaid borders that illuminate on hover, and crisp keyboard focus rings resembling physical metal clips.
anti_goals: No soft, blurry drop shadows (only hard, crisp 1px offsets).
No circular dial or radial progress indicators.

candidates.name: The Cartographic Desk
candidates.design_thesis: A desk-surface layout where the current leader is the central focal point, and options are stacked like physical index cards on a cartographer's workspace. It prioritizes immediate visual hierarchy and physical depth.
candidates.composition: A centered, single-column layout. At the top sits an oversized, double-bordered 'Leader Card' that commands attention. Below it, a compact grid of option cards features inline scoring buttons styled as physical brass rivets.
candidates.typography: Playfair Display for headers to project elegance, paired with a classic typewriter-style slab-serif for values and scores to feel like typed field notes.
candidates.interaction_emphasis: Focuses on tactile press-down states resembling physical brass buttons, subtle card-stacking depth using layered borders, and smooth fade-ins for newly calculated leaders.
anti_goals: No modern neon highlights or glowing active states.
No infinite scroll or paginated lists.
No sliding toggle switches or modern range sliders.
